best_for: Gaming groups and podcasters who want low-latency voice chat on a server they run themselves, on Windows or Linux.

points.title: You bring the server
points.text: Mumble is a client for a Mumble server. Anyone can host one and keep control of their own data, with fine-grained permissions, bots and links to existing user databases.

points.title: Built for low lag
points.text: The project's focus is low latency and clear audio. Traffic is always encrypted, and users sign in with key pairs by default rather than passwords.

points.title: Hear players where they stand
points.text: Positional audio places voices by in-game position, and an overlay shows who is talking. A multi-channel recorder helps podcasters edit each voice separately.

points.title: Free and BSD-licensed
points.text: There is no price and no account to buy. The code is under the BSD 3-Clause license.

points.title: The Mac build is stuck at 1.5.901
points.text: The project says it can no longer build Mac binaries for the 1.5 series, because its build Mac now runs macOS 26, which removed a framework Qt 5 needs. Homebrew disabled its cask in September 2026 after it failed Gatekeeper checks. Arm64 Mac builds return with the 1.6 release candidates.

points.title: Upgrading from 1.3 or older
points.text: The download page says the upgrade path from 1.3.x is broken, so uninstall the old client before you install 1.5.

points.title: Packages and versions
points.text: Windows gets a machine-wide x64 installer, and the Windows listing keeps 11 versions. The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub for x64 and Arm64. macOS and Linux list only the current release.
